verses.1: Ask the LORD for rain in the season of the early and late rains. The LORD makes clouds and will give them rain, each one grass in the field.
verses.2: For the diviners have spoken lies, the seers have had false visions, and the dreamers tell hollow dreams, they comfort with emptiness. Therefore they are scattered like sheep, they are distressed, because there is no shepherd.
verses.3: My anger is kindled against the shepherds, and I will hold the flock to account. For the LORD of Hosts is watching over His flock, the house of Judah, and will set them like a stately horse in battle.
verses.4: From Him comes the cornerstone, from Him the nail, from Him the battle bow, from Him every one who rises up is together.
verses.5: And they will be like mighty men treading the mortar in the streets of war, and they will fight, for the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses will be put to shame.
verses.6: I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back, for I have compassion on them, and they will be as those whom I did not cast off, for I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
verses.7: And they will be like warriors of Ephraim, and their hearts will rejoice as with wine, and their children will see and rejoice, their hearts will exult in the LORD.
verses.8: I will sow them among the peoples, and they will remember me, and their children will live and return.
verses.9: I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and from Assyria, and I will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and there will be none left among them.
verses.10: And they will cross the sea in trouble, and strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the rivers will dry up, and the pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will be removed.
verses.11: And they will pass through the narrow sea, and strike the sea's waves, and all the riverbeds will dry up, and the pride of Assyria will be brought low, and the staff of Egypt will be taken away.
verses.12: I will make them strong in the LORD, and in His name they will walk, says the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "early and late rains" — the Hebrew uses מָטָר and מַלְקוֹשׁ, both referring to seasonal rains.
- v. 11: "the narrow sea" — the Septuagint reads "narrow sea," but the Hebrew uses צָרָה, meaning "narrow" or "troubled," not specifying a known body of water.
- v. 12: "in His name" — the Hebrew uses בְּשְׁמוֹ, which could be read as "in His name" or "by His name," but the former is more natural in context.
raw:
[1] Ask the LORD for rain in the season of the early and late rains. The LORD makes clouds and will give them rain, each one grass in the field.

[2] For the diviners have spoken lies, the seers have had false visions, and the dreamers tell hollow dreams, they comfort with emptiness. Therefore they are scattered like sheep, they are distressed, because there is no shepherd.

[3] My anger is kindled against the shepherds, and I will hold the flock to account. For the LORD of Hosts is watching over His flock, the house of Judah, and will set them like a stately horse in battle.

[4] From Him comes the cornerstone, from Him the nail, from Him the battle bow, from Him every one who rises up is together.

[5] And they will be like mighty men treading the mortar in the streets of war, and they will fight, for the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses will be put to shame.

[6] I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back, for I have compassion on them, and they will be as those whom I did not cast off, for I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.

[7] And they will be like warriors of Ephraim, and their hearts will rejoice as with wine, and their children will see and rejoice, their hearts will exult in the LORD.

[8] I will sow them among the peoples, and they will remember me, and their children will live and return.

[9] I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and from Assyria, and I will bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and there will be none left among them.

[10] And they will cross the sea in trouble, and strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the rivers will dry up, and the pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will be removed.

[11] And they will pass through the narrow sea, and strike the sea's waves, and all the riverbeds will dry up, and the pride of Assyria will be brought low, and the staff of Egypt will be taken away.

[12] I will make them strong in the LORD, and in His name they will walk, says the LORD.

---
Notes
- v. 1: "early and late rains" — the Hebrew uses מָטָר and מַלְקוֹשׁ, both referring to seasonal rains.
- v. 11: "the narrow sea" — the Septuagint reads "narrow sea," but the Hebrew uses צָרָה, meaning "narrow" or "troubled," not specifying a known body of water.
- v. 12: "in His name" — the Hebrew uses בְּשְׁמוֹ, which could be read as "in His name" or "by His name," but the former is more natural in context.
